description: Run a script on Windows instance to prepare for Memory acquisition.

AccessKeyId.description: (Required) AccesskeyID to store evidence details in S3.

SecretAccessKey.description: (Required) SecretAccessKey to store evidence details in S3

SessionToken.description: (Required) SessionToken to store evidence details in S3.

runCommand: # $ErrorActionPreference is deliberately left at its default. Windows Server
# ships PowerShell 5.1, where setting it to 'Stop' turns anything a native
# executable writes to stderr into a terminating error - and `aws s3 cp`
# writes its progress there, so the upload would abort despite succeeding.
# The explicit $LASTEXITCODE checks below are what make this script fail
# honestly, and they do not have that hazard.
# Every step below is checked. This script previously ended in an
# unconditional 'exit 0' with no check on winpmem or on either upload, so a
# Windows acquisition that captured nothing still reported Success and the
# investigation only failed later, when it could not find the capture.
function Fail($message) { Write-Output "MEMORY_ACQUISITION_FAILED: $message"; exit 1 }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path C:\forensic-analysis | Out-Null
Set-Location C:\forensic-analysis
$env:AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="{{ AccessKeyId }}"
$env:AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="{{ SecretAccessKey }}"
# No leading space inside these quotes. The session token was previously
# assigned as " {{ SessionToken }}", which STS rejects, so both uploads at
# the end of this script failed on every run.
$env:AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="{{ SessionToken }}"
$env:AWS_DEFAULT_REGION="{{ Region }}"
# The credentials are deliberately not echoed. SSM streams this output to
# CloudWatch Logs, and the previous revision printed the STS secret access
# key there on every acquisition.
Start-Process -FilePath "msiexec.exe" -ArgumentList "/i https://awscli.amazonaws.com/AWSCLIV2.msi /qn" -Wait
$env:Path=[System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine")
aws sts get-caller-identity | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail 'the supplied credentials are not usable - refusing to capture memory that cannot be uploaded' }
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
# NOTE: winpmem is fetched from GitHub over TLS and run as SYSTEM on the
# instance under investigation with no signature or digest check. Pin a
# known good SHA256 here, or stage the binary in the forensic bucket next to
# the LiME modules, before relying on this in an untrusted network.
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri  https://github.com/Velocidex/WinPmem/releases/download/v4.0.rc1/winpmem_mini_x64_rc2.exe -OutFile winp.exe
if (-not (Test-Path winp.exe) -or (Get-Item winp.exe).Length -eq 0) { Fail 'downloading winpmem failed' }
.\winp.exe output.raw
# winpmem's exit code is NOT a success signal. The pinned winpmem_mini build
# reports itself as version 2.0.1 and exits 1 even after a complete
# acquisition - verified on Windows Server 2019, where it wrote a 9.5 GB image
# and still returned 1. Checking it aborted every Windows acquisition,
# including the ones that worked. The artefact is the signal instead: on
# Windows Server 2022 the same binary's driver unloads immediately and leaves
# output.raw at 0 bytes, which the checks below reject.
$physical = (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).TotalPhysicalMemory
if (-not (Test-Path output.raw)) { Fail 'winpmem produced no output.raw at all' }
$captured = (Get-Item output.raw).Length
Write-Output "captured $captured bytes of $physical bytes of physical memory"
if ($captured -eq 0) { Fail 'the memory capture is 0 bytes - winpmem could not load its driver on this Windows build' }
# A RAW image is physical memory plus padding, so it is never much smaller
# than RAM. Half is a floor that catches a truncated capture without
# rejecting a legitimate one.
if ($physical -and $captured -lt ($physical / 2)) { Fail "the memory capture is only $captured bytes for $physical bytes of RAM - refusing to upload a truncated capture as evidence" }
CertUtil -hashfile .\output.raw SHA256 > raw_sha256.txt
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail 'hashing the memory capture failed' }
aws s3 cp output.raw {{s3ArtifactLocation}}/
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail 'uploading the memory capture to S3 failed' }
aws s3 cp raw_sha256.txt {{s3ArtifactLocation}}/
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail 'uploading the memory capture hash to S3 failed' }
echo 's3 cp complete'
exit 0;
